subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured `skills.entries.<skill>.env` credential-shaped keys bypass the generic sensitive-name block for that active skill's host run while dangerous host override names remain blocked?
rationale: The source-backed bug is clear, but the fix changes a credential-to-exec boundary and overlaps the inverse skill-secret leak issue, so automation should not choose the permanent security contract alone.

options.title: Allow configured skill env secrets
options.body: Permit keys explicitly present in the active skill config to pass the sensitive-name check, with tests for dangerous-name rejection, gog-like credential delivery, and unrelated exec isolation.

options.title: Keep metadata-only sensitive allowlist
options.body: Require each sensitive env key to be declared in skill metadata, then update docs or doctor guidance so users do not expect arbitrary credential-shaped `env` keys to work.

options.title: Define a separate credential contract
options.body: Defer the bypass and design a SecretRef or plugin-owned credential path for CLI skills that need headless auth.

recommendation.title: Allow configured skill env secrets
recommendation.body: Permit keys explicitly present in the active skill config to pass the sensitive-name check, with tests for dangerous-name rejection, gog-like credential delivery, and unrelated exec isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history in the overlapping skill env, SecretRef, release, and current-main paths.
